taxonomyNote: NatureServe lists P. alleghaniensis as Eastern Ratsnake, while New York DEC (2025) calls it the central ratsnake and treats yellow ratsnake P. quadrivittatus as a separate eastern-clade species; Burbrink et al. and the NY assessment note hybridization and unresolved boundaries.
behavior: Diurnal in spring and fall and nocturnal in summer; active late April to October in the north.
Proficient climber and swimmer; eats birds and eggs, small mammals, lizards, frogs; adults eat mainly endotherms, young mainly ectotherms.
Emerges from hibernacula mid-April to early June; overwinters communally in rocky talus, ledges, basements, cisterns and wells, and may migrate between hibernaculum and summer range.
habitat: Mix of open and wooded land: hardwood forest, old fields, farmland near woods, barnyards and rural buildings; hibernates in deep crevices or underground.
range: East of the Mississippi River to the Atlantic Seaboard Fall Line in Virginia, north to Wisconsin, Michigan, New York, Vermont, Massachusetts, and the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Quebec.
aliases: Black ratsnake (former name Elaphe o. obsoleta)
